subject: Transfer control playbook, signing cadence & technical evidence attachments
messages:
From: Emily Clarke <emily.clarke@heronhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@heronhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: initial privacy / transfer questions for upcoming eval

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profiles. Before procurement can move forward we need to confirm a few items related to cross-border processing for our EU patients:

- Do you rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for EU transfers, and do you include the UK IDTA / UK Addendum in your DPA?
- We need a scoped Treatment Impact Assessment (TIA) or DTIA for telemetry and inference logs that may leave the EU. Can you provide the proposed TIA boundaries (what leaves region, what is pseudonymized, retention windows)?
- Can you share the current subprocessor list and the locations of KMS keys used for on-call recovery? Procurement will need a CSV processor map, and legal will want an HSM/KMS attestation if keys are outside the EU/UK.

Attached is a simple worksheet with the data categories we collect — procurement asked that we get a DPA redline and a TIA scope by end of next week.

Appreciate a quick confirmation of the signing cadence (DocuSign vs countersigned PDF) and whether Redwood can provide evidence for the UK Addendum artifacts.

Best,
Emily
Emily Clarke
VP, Product & Compliance
Heron Health

Attachments: Heron_TIA_scope_20260418.xlsx (spreadsheet), data_samples.csv (referenced)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Clarke <emily.clarke@heronhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transfer control playbook, signing cadence & technical evidence attachments

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear ask and the worksheet. Copying Kim and Laura for the technical and legal bits. Quick answers up front so procurement can triage:

1) DPA / Transfers: Redwood supports SCCs for EU transfers and includes the UK IDTA / UK Addendum where customers require it. We ship a DPA with both SCCs and a UK-addendum option; legal can provide the UK attestations and the standard Annex II mapping on request.

2) TIA / DTIA boundary: We can produce a scoped TIA for telemetry/inf logs. Our proposed scoping approach:
   - Inference request metadata (headers, timestamps) may be transmitted to control plane regions for routing and billing; model inputs are treated as customer content and handled per residency commitments.
   - Telemetry used for platform health (aggregated traces, anonymized error logs) will be pseudonymized, retention 30 days by default, can be reduced by contract.
   - KV cache backups and snapshot logs (diagnostic) stay in-region for customers with residency requirements, with optional on-prem/edge export.

3) Subprocessors & KMS: We maintain a live CSV of subprocessors; Kim, can you attach the processor map and note which subprocessors have access to encryption keys?

4) Signing cadence: We typically do DocuSign for standard DPAs. For enterprise counter-signed addenda we can accept uploaded PDFs. Laura — legal prefers DocuSign envelope for standard flows; please confirm.

I'll follow up with a short technical packet and the redlined DPA. If your legal wants a one-hour walk-through of the TIA scoping next week we can schedule.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Director, GTM Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Emily Clarke <emily.clarke@heronhealth.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transfer control playbook, signing cadence & technical evidence attachments

Emily — attaching the processor map and a short technical memo. Highlights below; see attachments for CSV and proposed TIA scope workbook.

- Subprocessors: current list attached (processor_map_heron_v1.csv). Only three subprocessors handle tokenization/metrics outside of Redwood: CloudMetrics Ltd. (metrics aggregation, EU region with EU-hosted nodes), EdgeOps Inc. (optional burst footprint in us-east-1), and LogStore GmbH (long-term logs archiving — EU-based S3). We can provide processing agreements for each on request.

- KMS / HSM: Customer data keys (CDKs) are tenant-specific. By default, CDKs are stored in our managed KMS; for enterprise customers we offer a customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) hosted in their preferred cloud region. Currently, the backup and disaster-recovery keys used for cross-region failover are stored in our HSM pool in us-west-2; if you require a UK/EU-only KMS footprint we can gate DR keys and provide an HSM attestation.

- TIA specifics (summary):
   * What may leave EU/UK: aggregated telemetry (1:1000 sampled traces), anonymized error stacks, billing metadata (token counts, region).
   * What stays in-region: customer payloads for pinned-residency customers, KV cache snapshots if residency flag enabled.
   * Retention: default telemetry retention 30 days; logs archived to EU LogStore if EU residency is requested.

Attachments included: processor_map_heron_v1.csv (CSV), proposed_TIA_scope_notes.txt (short memo), redlined_DPA_diego_20260418.pdf (PDF with inline comments).

Please review the redlines (I highlighted the UK Addendum checkbox and the KMS BR section). Happy to jump on a quick call with procurement to walk through the processor map.

Best,
Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
